title: Novel images raised visual cortex responses of RS, FS and Vip units but not of Sst units, which fell at 20-70 ms, in 71 mice of Allen Visual Behavior Neuropixels
abstract: Slice and EM wiring show a disinhibitory chain in cortex: Vip cells inhibit Sst cells, which inhibit pyramidal cells. We tested whether image novelty changes spiking of cell classes in the sign pattern that this wiring predicts. We used Allen Visual Behavior Neuropixels (153 sessions, 81 mice). In each unit we compared responses to 6 non-shared images with responses to 2 shared images, in Novel minus Familiar sessions. Optotagging identified Sst units (31 mice) and Vip units (18 mice). In visual cortex of 71 G-trained mice (active block, 20-250 ms, log rate ratio, 95% mouse-bootstrap interval), novelty increased regular-spiking units by +0.27 [0.25, 0.30], fast-spiking units by +0.48 [0.43, 0.52] and Vip units by +0.59 [0.35, 0.89]. Sst units did not increase (+0.03 [-0.05, 0.09]); at 20-70 ms they decreased (-0.21 [-0.29, -0.13]). At 70-150 ms, regular-spiking rate rose 49% while Sst rate did not change. LGd showed no effect and LP a small one, so the effect appears between thalamus and V1; inside cortex it did not grow along the anatomical hierarchy (V1 largest for regular-spiking units). The passive replay block gave the same pattern. The pattern fits Vip-to-Sst disinhibition and does not fit a pure feedforward drive increase. But the early Sst decrease began at about 35 ms, before a detectable Vip increase, so the timing does not show that Vip causes it. Limitations: for Sst and Vip units novelty is confounded with image set (only G-trained Cre mice; for RS/FS the image-set term was 0.02-0.07), Vip units are few (81), and the wiring argument uses connection signs, not a fitted circuit model. Code, the unit table, statistics and figures are included.

A: mean normalized flash responses in Familiar sessions. B: novelty effect over time with 95% mouse-bootstrap bands. RS, FS and Vip effects rise from about 50-65 ms; the Sst effect is negative from about 35 to 100 ms and becomes positive only after about 115 ms.
Novelty effect by area against the Harris et al. (2019) hierarchy score. LGd has no effect and LP a small one. Inside cortex the RS effect is largest in V1 and does not increase along the hierarchy.

citations.reason: Allen Visual Behavior Neuropixels session NWB files and metadata (public S3 bucket) are the data of this study.

Nitzan et al. 2024 reported stronger novel-image responses in visual cortex and weaker ones in thalamus in the same data; we confirm this with a within-unit contrast and extend it to optotagged classes.
